newsitem.title: FRANCE: French court upholds Socialist council convictions.
newsitem.headline: French court upholds Socialist council convictions.

text.p: A French appeals court on Thursday upheld sentences for two Socialist members of the Strasbourg city council condemned to one-year suspended prison terms for receiving illegal corporate favours.

The court in the eastern city also upheld a lower court's decision in February to fine Jean Oehler 50,000 francs ($9,500) and Jean-Pierre Freani 30,000 francs ($5,700) for receiving benefits from units of building group Bouygues.
Oehler, 58 and a former member of parliament, was also stripped of his right to hold public office for three years.

Oehler, an elected official in charge of social housing, was found guilty of having underpaid for work done at his house by Bouygues unit Kessler. Oehler said he had protested to Kessler against the low bill as soon as he noticed the discrepancy.

Freani, 45, was faulted for being on the payroll of Bouygues while he was an elected member of a commission which awarded public works contracts. Freani was the one and only employee of Bouygues unit Sirmad-est and received a 30,000 francs ($5,700) monthly salary.
Oehler said he would make a final appeal to France's supreme court, the Cour de Cassation. Freani said he was dropping legal action "despite a feeling of injustice". ($1=5.270 French Franc)
